argument:
Solarvest's RM2.371bn order book, 13.2% latest-quarter revenue growth and improved 12.2% margin support a project-conversion purchase scenario. FY26 CFO turned positive at RM90.560m, leaving RM32.112m after PP&E and intangibles before expansion investments. The March balance showed substantial cash, deposits and short investments against RM411.845m borrowings, providing historical funding capacity rather than a claim about June liquidity.

Quarterly EPS fell to 1.99 sen despite 19.8% profit growth, exposing dilution; equity/warrant/ESOP funding contributed RM386.821m in FY26. Expansion outlays exceeded the simple cash surplus, and latest full cash/debt statements remain inaccessible. At 48x trailing and estimated 25.24x forward earnings, the buy case requires order conversion to outrun share dilution and funding costs. Strong trend supplies interest, but overbought RSI limits tactical conviction. Neither management's conversion target nor backlog is realised owner cash.
key_points: Order book, revenue and margin improvement support execution upside.
Older measured cash generation and liquidity provide explicitly dated financing context.
Dilution and valuation require growth in per-share cash, not headline profits alone.
